question: Should OpenClaw add a read-only recursive/depth mode to `subagents list`, and should it live on the existing subagents tool/slash command or wait for the broader session-chain/tree API design?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines public tool and slash-command semantics for nested agent visibility and must preserve the existing subagent control boundary.

options.title: Add Read-Only Depth Listing
options.body: Add an additive depth/recursive option to `subagents` that returns descendant rows with parent/depth metadata while leaving mutation scope direct-child-only.

options.title: Route Through Chain/Tree Work
options.body: Keep this issue open but make recursive visibility depend on the broader session-chain or active-agent tree design before adding another public shape.

options.title: Decline Hierarchy Expansion
options.body: Treat depth-0 inspection of depth-2 workers as outside the current core direction and document existing direct-child and `sessions_history` workflows instead.

recommendation.title: Add Read-Only Depth Listing
recommendation.body: Add an additive depth/recursive option to `subagents` that returns descendant rows with parent/depth metadata while leaving mutation scope direct-child-only.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision extends the nested subagent behavior and tool surface introduced in `b8f66c260db8`.
